sections.h2: How does a deed get recorded in Lake County, Ohio?
sections.html:
It takes two counters in Painesville. The Transfer Office (the Auditor's first floor) comes first, where you complete an Exempt Form or a Conveyance Fee Form and get the deed stamped. The Recorder, on the lower level of the Administration Building, comes second and processes the deed on the spot.

The recorder's contact page gives the street address as 105 Main Street, Lower Level, with P.O. Box 490, Painesville, OH 44077, phone (440) 350-2510 and email recorder@lakecountyohio.gov. Counter service runs weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m., closed on holidays, and the fee page asks that the day's last recordings be in before 3:45.

A mailed filing has its own checklist. Each auditor and engineer stamp has to be on the deed already, and the envelope needs a cover letter, one check for the Recorder, one for the Auditor and a stamped return envelope. If the Auditor's stamp is missing, the deed comes back rejected.

sections.h2: What does the Lake County Recorder charge, and what goes to the Auditor?
sections.html:
The Recorder bills $34.00 for a two page deed and $5.00 for preservation, and each page past the second adds $8.00. The Auditor collects its own transfer charges, which is why the office wants two checks.

Lake County deed charges listed on the Recorder's guidelines and record-a-deed pages and on the Auditor's transfer page
ItemPrinted amountPayee
Deed up to two pages$34.00 plus a $5.00 preservation feeRecorder
Each page after two$8.00Recorder
Reference to an earlier recorded document$4.00 apieceRecorder
Nonconforming document$20.00 penaltyRecorder
Conveyance fee$4.00 per $1,000 of valueAuditor
Transfer fee$0.50 for each parcelAuditor

Per the Auditor's FAQ, the $4.00 breaks into a $1.00 state share and a $3.00 county share, the county piece set by a commissioners' resolution dated March 26, 1990 under section 322.02.

sections.h2: What paperwork does the Lake County Auditor want with a transfer?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate FAQ answers the common questions. Either side of the deal, or a representative, may hand in the deed, and mail is accepted. Everything must be complete, signed and notarized. The Transfer Office takes transfers between 8 and 4.

  • A DTE 100 or DTE 100EX goes with every transfer.
  • Parcels in the homestead or CAUV farm programs need a notarized DTE 101 or DTE 102 first.
  • A sale of anything short of a whole platted sublot, such as a piece of a sublot or a metes and bounds tract, must clear the Tax Map Department. Exempt transfers skip that stop.
  • Taking someone off a deed means drafting a new deed, and the FAQ points owners toward a title company or attorney.

The county posts owner names exactly as the recorded deed spells them, so a typo on the deed travels into the tax records.

sections.h2: Which Lake County transfers are exempt from the conveyance fee?
sections.html:
Section 319.54(G)(3) holds the exemption list, and the reason is written on the form that section 319.202 requires. Examples that fit house sales:

  • A deed given only as security for a debt, or releasing that security.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • Survivorship transfers under sections 5302.17 or 5302.18.
  • A deed to a trustee when the maker kept an unlimited power to revoke.
  • A transfer to a non-dealer who is only a stop on the way to a prompt resale.

One shortcut shows on the Recorder's page: a Transfer on Death Beneficiary Designation Affidavit skips the Auditor and goes straight to the Recorder, with the recording fee and a return envelope.

sections.h2: Can a deed be e-recorded in Lake County?
sections.html:
Yes. The Record A Deed page names four e-recording partners: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hop Docs. You deal with one of those firms, because the Recorder's office does not operate the portal itself.

For research, the Recorder's e-recording page points to the AVA search engine for basic results and to Laredo Select for deeper searching, which needs a registered account. Filings cannot carry watermarks. The office's services menu also lists a property fraud alert and a video chat on that topic.

sections.h2: How should a Lake County deed be prepared?
sections.html:
The Recorder's guidelines restate section 317.114 and warn that a deed outside them is still accepted but costs the $20.00 penalty. Before signing, confirm:

  • Type at 10 point or bigger, on paper cut between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14.
  • Black or blue ink, with nothing highlighted.
  • One inch margins at the sides and foot, three inches clear at the top of page one for stamps, and an inch and a half on the pages after.
  • A title, a date, typed names and titles under every signature, and a notary block that shows the commission expiration.
  • The preparer's name and a full legal description.

When one document refers to an earlier one, cite its number, or its book and page, along with the recording date. Each such reference adds $4.00.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Lake County for a home sale?
sections.html:
Lake County lies on the southern shore of Lake Erie inside the Cleveland metropolitan area. Painesville is the seat and Mentor the largest city. Formed March 6, 1840, it has 227 square miles of land inside a 979 square mile total, and its lakeshore runs 31 miles. Former glacial beaches survive as ridge roads such as South Ridge, and Lake Shore Boulevard follows another old beach through Mentor Township.

Census QuickFacts: 232,217 residents in mid 2025 (roughly 1,014 per square mile) and 107,571 housing units. Ownership rate, 75.8 percent. Median value of owned homes, $214,100. Median gross rent, $1,113. Median household income, $80,925. Interstates and routes matter to buyers here: I-90 and State Route 2 run through, State Route 44 links them, and Laketran buses reach downtown Cleveland.

School district names carry weight in listings. Mentor Public, Painesville City Local, Willoughby-Eastlake City, Wickliffe City, Kirtland Local, Madison Local, Perry Local, Riverside Local and Fairport Harbor Exempted Village each cover part of the county.

sections.h2: What tax questions come up at a Lake County closing?
sections.html:
The Treasurer lists the 2026 tax payable in 2027 as due February 24 and July 21, 2027 for real estate, and bills mail out in mid-January and mid-June, per the Auditor's FAQ. A buyer's lender or the title company will ask for the status of those halves, so request the Treasurer's payoff before the closing date. The Treasurer's billing line is (440) 350-2516, and the Auditor's real estate staff answer address and credit questions at (440) 350-2532.

If a record shows a wrong owner address, the Auditor corrects owner addresses while the Treasurer handles the tax mailing address, so changes may need two calls.

faqs.q: Where is the Lake County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: Lower Level, 105 Main Street, Painesville, OH 44077, with mail going to P.O. Box 490. The listed number is (440) 350-2510 and counter hours run weekdays from 8 to 4, closed on holidays.

faqs.q: What is the Lake County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: $4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price plus $0.50 per parcel, according to the Auditor's Real Estate FAQ. It is paid to the Auditor before the Recorder sees the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need two checks to record a deed in Lake County?
faqs.a: Yes. The guidelines want a check for each office, one made out to the Lake County Recorder and one to the Lake County Auditor. Mailed filings also need a stamped self-addressed envelope, or the originals come back collect on delivery.

faqs.q: When does a Lake County sale need Tax Map approval?
faqs.a: When money changes hands and the parcel is anything other than a full sublot in a platted subdivision. Part of a sublot and metes and bounds tracts both qualify. Exempt transfers do not need it.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Lake County Auditor?
faqs.a: Yes, mail transfers are accepted. Address them to the Auditor's Real Estate Transfer Office, 105 Main Street, PO Box 490, Painesville, OH 44077. The deed is passed to the Recorder after transfer.
